hints: Look at the Period 3 oxide trend, from basic on the left to acidic on the right, and remember only one element forms an amphoteric oxide.
Y must be aluminium, and for X focus on which +4 oxide is soluble and acidic, $\text{SiO}_2$ is insoluble while $\text{SO}_2$ dissolves readily.
Now combine $\text{Al}^{3+}$ with $\text{S}^{2-}$ and balance the charges to get a neutral formula for Z.
walkthrough:
**Identify Y from the amphoteric oxide**

In Period 3, sodium and magnesium oxides are basic, silicon to sulfur oxides are acidic, but aluminium oxide is special.

$$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 \text{ is amphoteric}$$ 
So Y is aluminium, $\text{Al}$.

**Identify X from the +4 soluble acidic oxide**

X has oxidation number +4 in its oxide, so the oxide is $\text{XO}_2$. In Period 3 the +4 candidates are mainly Si and S.

$$\text{Si (+4) gives SiO}_2, \quad \text{S (+4) gives SO}_2$$
$\text{SiO}_2$ is acidic but insoluble in water, while $\text{SO}_2$ is acidic and soluble, forming sulfurous acid. So X is sulfur, $\text{S}$.

**Combine Al and S to make neutral compound Z**

Aluminium is in Group 13, so it forms $\text{Al}^{3+}$. Sulfur is in Group 16, so it forms $\text{S}^{2-}$.

To balance charge: $2 \times (+3) + 3 \times (-2) = 0$
$$\text{Al}_2\text{S}_3$$
This is the formula of compound Z.

options.A: AlP would need X to be phosphorus. Phosphorus forms acidic oxides but its common soluble acidic oxides have P in +3 or +5, not +4, so this does not fit the description of X.
options.B: This is correct. Y is Al from the amphoteric $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$, and X is S from the soluble acidic $\text{SO}_2$ where S is +4. Balancing $\text{Al}^{3+}$ and $\text{S}^{2-}$ gives $\text{Al}_2\text{S}_3$.
options.C: Si2P5 is wrong on both counts. Si forms an insoluble $\text{SiO}_2$, not a soluble oxide, and P does not show +4 in its normal acidic oxide. The formula itself also does not balance normal Si and P ion charges.
options.D: SiS2 pairs Si with S, but neither element fits Y. Y must be the amphoteric oxide former, which is Al, not Si. This option ignores the amphoteric clue completely.
